text: Writing clean code is a skill that separates good programmers from great ones. At its heart, clean code is about readability—making sure that anyone, including your future self, can understand what the code does without struggling. One of the first steps is to follow clear naming conventions. Variables and functions should have descriptive names, like `calculateTotalPrice` instead of `a` or `x`. This simple habit can save hours of confusion later. Another key principle is keeping functions short and focused. A function should do only one thing well. If you find a function performing several tasks, it’s time to break it into smaller, logical pieces. This approach not only makes the code easier to test but also significantly improves its maintainability. When you return to a project after months away, clean code feels like a friendly guide, not a puzzle. Ultimately, writing clean code is a matter of respect—for yourself, your teammates, and the software you build together.
